na_rules.reason: Temporal contrast queries require a temporal graph class: a pulse, sustained, temporal-conditional or temporal-mediation contrast is indexed by a lag and a horizon, and a static graph class has no time index for either.

Static queries do not denote on TemporalDag, TemporalCpdag, or TemporalPag. TemporalPag stays the equivalence class only for the temporal queries licensed on it. Latent confounding over time denotes on TemporalAdmg. An AverageEffect on a temporal graph denotes the lag-0 contrast and is a refused, executing cell (parity/support_closed.toml).
TransportQuery and InterferenceQuery are typed against static graphs; they do not denote on a temporal graph class.
cheap and full denote the ATE-shaped scalar refuter suite; a function-valued curve has no such state.
cheap and full denote the ATE-shaped scalar refuter suite; a graph-posterior response remains function-valued or atom-mixed with no licensed scalar-refuter state.
Unknown-tier cells license the two-scenario AverageEffect envelope only.
CoDetermined cells license AverageEffect and joint InterventionResponse only.
Tier-rule backgrounds are an explicit structure source.
cheap and full name the ATE-shaped scalar refuter suite; CoDetermined joint IR and the Unknown envelope have no licensed scalar-refuter state.

closed_rules.reason: An AverageEffect on one series (or event series) under a temporal graph denotes the lag-0 contrast E[Y_t | do(X_t = active)] - E[Y_t | do(X_t = control)]. The build compiles it as the pulse at offset 0 read at horizon 1: on a TemporalCpdag every completion adjusts for the parents of X_t (temporal backdoor), on a TemporalPag every MAG completion uses visibility-aware adjustment, and the Bayesian reading is the per-completion conjugate posterior with draw-wise identified-set bounds. Over a graph posterior the same pulse is compiled and the per-atom proofs mix as for any temporal pulse. The result keeps support status refused and discloses estimate.temporal_class.lag_zero_average_effect; no evidence row or coverage record names the cell. Effect modifiers, a non-mean functional and a population other than AllObserved are refused (next attempt: TemporalConditionalPulse or a temporal ResponseCurve).

Bayesian InterventionResponse cheap and full run the Bayesian refuter state on the intervention level and stay unlicensed: no evidence row or coverage record names the state. Cheap runs plugin-level overlap on the posterior-mean level and the prior and posterior predictive checks of the outcome regression; full adds plugin-level sampling stability, level-native prior sensitivity (the response is refitted at each prior-grid point and its posterior-mean level read back) and MCMC diagnostics. A graph posterior runs the plugin-level suite on the pooled level and the posterior checks on its primary identified atom. Requested explicitly, the state executes; the default suite still downgrades to the licensed validation none.

Derivative, elasticity and Jacobian cheap and full run the derivative refuter state and stay unlicensed: no evidence row or coverage record names it. Cheap checks support at the evaluation point and the central finite difference of the identified intervention levels against the published derivative on its reported scale (point derivatives of order one, order two on the identity scale, and observed-law average derivatives through ± shift interventions); full adds a whole-procedure row bootstrap of the derivative under independent subjects (the published value must lie in the replicates' 95% range; failed replicates are kept). Bayesian studies add the prior and posterior predictive checks of the outcome regression and, under full, prior sensitivity refitting the whole derivative at each grid point and MCMC diagnostics. ATE-shaped contrast refuters do not apply.

Temporal derivative, elasticity and Jacobian cheap and full run the temporal derivative refuter state and stay unlicensed: no evidence row or coverage record names it. The derivative is the slope of the linear unfolded fit at one horizon; the state checks support at the evaluation point, compares an identity-scale first derivative with the unit-step difference of the identified levels (the completion-weighted Pulse witness effect), and runs the TemporalDag Pulse-native suite on each identified completion's Pulse witness at that horizon (overlap, temporal placebo and pre-period checks; full adds circular-block stability). Bayesian studies add each witness's predictive checks and, under full, prior sensitivity. Completions are not mixed.

Temporal and class-aware InterventionResponse cheap and full run a refuter state and stay unlicensed: no evidence row or coverage record names it. A TemporalDag level runs the TemporalDag Pulse-native suite on each requested horizon's own Pulse witness (the unit contrast at that horizon with the response's intervention as the active arm, under that horizon's proof and lag indexer): overlap, the temporal placebo and pre-period checks, and under full circular-block stability under the dependent-series design; Bayesian studies add the predictive checks and prior sensitivity of each witness; horizons are not mixed. A Cpdag or Pag level runs the plugin-level suite on every completion's own level and estimand (overlap; full adds per-completion sampling stability), mixes the reports only when every completion answers the same level, and reports how far the completions disagree.

TemporalCpdag and TemporalPag InterventionResponse cheap and full run the class temporal refuter state and stay unlicensed: no evidence row or coverage record names it. Every identified completion at every requested horizon is checked on its own Pulse witness (the unit contrast with the level's intervention as the active arm, under that completion's proof and lag indexer) with the TemporalDag Pulse-native suite (overlap, temporal placebo and pre-period checks; full adds circular-block stability); Bayesian studies add each witness's predictive checks and prior sensitivity. Completions and horizons are not mixed; a per-horizon disagreement diagnostic reports how far the completions' witness effects spread.

Bayesian joint InterventionResponse on a CoDetermined tier closure runs response.bayesian over the closure's generalized adjustment set (the same tier identification the Frequentist cell.aipw cell uses) and stays unlicensed: no evidence row or coverage record names it. The outcome regression is additive in the treatments, so the published level is that model's joint level, not the saturated cell mean cell.aipw estimates.
Counterfactual requires a supplied static Dag.

Derivatives, elasticities, directional derivatives and Jacobians on a supplied Cpdag, Pag, Admg or TemporalAdmg (read as its contemporaneous ADMG projection) execute through the compiler and stay unlicensed: no evidence row or coverage record names them. Each identified completion of a Cpdag or Pag (every DAG of the Markov class, every MAG completion of a PAG read as its most-confounded ADMG) is identified by one adjustment set valid for every treatment/outcome pair the functional names, and the continuous response estimator the functional selects (local-polynomial point derivative, Riesz average derivative, additive-GAM Jacobian and directional derivative, or the Bayesian response) is fitted on that set; completions that share an adjustment set share one fit, and completions that disagree publish the identified set of their values with no mixed band. An Admg with bidirected edges is identified by the adjustment criterion on its proper back-door graph, so a latent common cause stays in the graph; an Admg without them runs the Dag route. A completion that ID identifies only through a non-adjustment functional (front-door) is accounted as unevaluable mass because no continuous-treatment estimator evaluates such a functional, and a pair with a hedge is refused with its certificate (Shpitser and Pearl 2006). Frequentist intervals are the estimator's own sampling intervals and Bayesian intervals are credible intervals of the response posterior. Cheap and full validation and graph-posterior structures are refused.

Cheap and full derivative validation and graph-posterior derivative mixtures on a Cpdag, Pag, Admg or TemporalAdmg are refused: the derivative refuter states run on a supplied Dag, and a posterior over structures has no single adjustment set to difference.
graph-posterior structures are refused: a path, distribution, or mediation mixture is not a single estimand across posterior atoms.
Accepted InterventionalDistribution is licensed on Dag and Admg; Cpdag/Pag remain refused.
MediationEffect requires a supplied static Dag.
AnomalyAttribution and ChangeAttribution require a supplied static Dag. The attribution engine has no lagged latent slice.
Attribution is licensed only for an explicit Dag at validation none.
Attribution has no native refuter suite; ATE refuters do not apply.
AnomalyAttribution and ChangeAttribution on a time graph require an explicit TemporalDag.
Temporal attribution is licensed only for an explicit TemporalDag at validation none.
Temporal attribution has no native refuter suite; ATE refuters do not apply.

A TransportQuery on a Dag reads the Dag as the selection diagram of a model with no latent confounding: its ADMG embedding (every edge directed, no bidirected edge) with the declared selection nodes, identified by the same implemented sID subset (Direct, or an S-admissible standardization) and estimated by the same trial-to-target weighting of the supplied selection and treatment probabilities, with the delta-method (or Newey-West on one series) interval frequentist and the Dirichlet trial-row posterior Bayesian. Cheap and full run the transport-native suite (calibration of the supplied probabilities against the rows they describe, effective sample size of the weights, and under full a whole-procedure bootstrap range). The result keeps support status refused; no evidence row or coverage record names the cell. Recursive sID outside the implemented subset is NotCertified.

A TransportQuery reads a selection diagram, which is an ADMG (a Dag is its confounder-free case). A Cpdag or Pag stands for several diagrams that can disagree on the transport formula, so it names no single diagram; the supplied-structure facade reports the per-member structural envelope. Next attempt: the Dag, Admg or TemporalAdmg the structure resolves to, or discovered_transport for the envelope. Recursive sID outside the implemented subset is NotCertified.

TransportQuery on an accepted Admg or TemporalAdmg executes the same sID identification and trial-to-target estimator as the explicit graph but no evidence row names the accepted-structure cell, so the result keeps support status refused. Cheap and full run the transport-native suite.
TransportQuery graph-posterior mixtures are not staged.

TransportQuery cheap and full run the transport-native suite and stay unlicensed: no evidence row or coverage record names the state. The supplied selection probabilities are tested against the observed trial count and the supplied treatment probabilities against the observed arm counts of the trial rows (Poisson-binomial z tests, with batch-means variance on one dependent series); the effective sample size of the selection-odds and arm weights is reported as a share of the trial rows; full adds a whole-procedure bootstrap of the transported contrast (rows, or circular blocks on one series) whose 95% percentile range must contain the published value. ATE-shaped contrast refuters do not apply. Requested explicitly, the state executes; the default suite still downgrades to the licensed validation none.

An InterferenceQuery on an accepted structure executes the same known-assignment exposure contrast as the explicit one, but no evidence row names the accepted-structure cell, so the result keeps support status refused.

An InterferenceQuery on an Admg, a TemporalAdmg read as its contemporaneous projection, a Cpdag or a Pag states the exposure contrast under that structure class. The contrast is identified by the known assignment mechanism and the exposure mapping on the fixed network (the assignment is independent of the potential outcomes by design, or by the supplied exposure probabilities and the declared network exchangeability), so no edge of the structure enters the identification: a latent confounder or an unresolved orientation in the structure cannot move it, and the structure binds only the unit schema (its width must equal the unit table's). The same procedures run as on a Dag: Young-bound Horvitz-Thompson/Hajek, cluster Neyman, exact two-stage saturation or supplied-propensity observational weighting with the sampling interval frequentist, and the conjugate Gaussian or cluster Dirichlet posterior Bayesian. The result keeps support status refused; no evidence row or coverage record names the cell.

InterferenceQuery on an Admg, TemporalAdmg, Cpdag or Pag executes unlicensed at validation none over a supplied or accepted structure (the rule above). Cheap and full have no interference-native refuter suite, and a graph posterior over these classes has no interference route. Next attempts: validation none over a supplied structure, or an explicit Dag at validation none.
InterferenceQuery graph-posterior mixtures are not staged.
InterferenceQuery has no native refuter suite; ATE refuters do not apply.

A ConditionalEffect on a TemporalAdmg reads tabular rows as the contemporaneous projection, which answers a different target than the temporal conditional contrast, so it is refused. The temporal conditional contrast is TemporalConditionalPulse or TemporalConditionalSustained on one series: it is identified by IDC on the unrolled window of the template and executes unlicensed (the TemporalAdmg rule below). The typed refusal names the next attempts: that temporal query on the series, TemporalConditionalPulse or TemporalConditionalSustained on a TemporalDag when the lag structure has no latent confounding, or the static Admg for the contemporaneous conditional effect.
ConditionalEffect on Admg is licensed for an explicit or accepted graph at validation none; graph-posterior mixing over Admg atoms is not staged.
ConditionalEffect on Admg is licensed at validation none only; cheap and full are not licensed: no refuter suite is staged for the IDC contrast over a modifier law.

A path-restricted natural effect on a supplied Pag is read through the ADMGs that share the m-separation model of each of its MAG completions, because a MAG fixes the latent projection only up to that model and a path-specific effect is not a function of it (T -> M -> Y, T -> Y has the same MAG with and without M <-> Y, yet the effect along T -> M -> Y is identified in one and has a recanting district in the other). The path-specific identifier decides every such ADMG on its own graph; the effect is reported only when every one is identified, as one estimate when they yield the same functional or as the identified set over the distinct functionals, and a single refused candidate refuses the effect: no functional is then correct for every model the Pag represents. A path-restricted natural effect on a supplied Cpdag is identified by the path-specific identifier in every DAG completion of the equivalence class and estimated by the same functional plug-in per identified completion: completions that identify the same effect keep that estimate and its uncertainty, completions that disagree publish the enumeration-weighted mean with the identified set over them, and a completion with a recanting witness is unidentified mass. A path-restricted natural effect on a supplied Admg (or the contemporaneous projection of a TemporalAdmg) is identified by the path-specific identifier over the mixed graph: the surgical total effect when every directed path is selected, the edge g-formula when the outcome's ancestors carry no latent confounding, and Shpitser's district formula (each district of the outcome's ancestors read at the treatment level of the edges that enter it, kernels from the complete ID algorithm) otherwise. A recanting district or a district kernel with a hedge is refused as not identified. The identified functional is evaluated by the finite-discrete functional plug-in (bootstrap interval) or its Bayesian-bootstrap posterior. The result keeps support status refused: no evidence row or coverage record names the cell, and cheap/full validation stays Dag-only.
Path and distribution queries execute only on a supplied static Dag or Admg; a directly supplied Pag hits the static-Dag/Admg requirement.
ADMG and TemporalAdmg InterventionalDistribution are licensed at validation none; cheap/full remain Dag-only.
Latent-confounded TemporalPag natural mediation is outside the existing cross-world identification theory; DAG-completion engineering cannot license it.

Frequentist graph-posterior mixing on DAG atoms is licensed for AverageEffect, ConditionalEffect, and static ResponseCurve/one-coordinate InterventionResponse. The listed static families remain unsupported.
Latent-confounded TemporalPag natural mediation is outside the existing cross-world identification theory; TemporalPag graph-posterior atoms are not mixed into a mediation envelope.
Distribution queries execute only on a supplied static Dag or Admg; a directly supplied Cpdag hits that requirement (Admg/Pag explicit already named above).
Query-native functional validation requires a Dag.
Graph-posterior derivative mixtures are not staged; the licensed derivative cells are Frequentist or Bayesian explicit or accepted Dag at validation none.
Graph-posterior mediation mixtures are not staged; the licensed MediationEffect cells are Frequentist or Bayesian explicit or accepted Dag.

The natural direct effect on a supplied Pag is the path-specific effect along the edges that avoid the mediator, read through the ADMGs that share the m-separation model of each MAG completion and reported only when every one is identified (one estimate for one functional, the identified set for several, a refusal when a candidate leaves it unidentified). The natural direct effect on a supplied Cpdag is the path-specific effect along the edges that avoid the mediator, identified in every DAG completion of the equivalence class and published as one estimate when the completions agree, or as the enumeration-weighted mean with the identified set when they disagree. The natural direct effect on a supplied Admg (or the contemporaneous projection of a TemporalAdmg) is the path-specific effect along the edges that avoid the mediator, identified by the path-specific identifier over the mixed graph (the edge g-formula without latent confounding on the outcome's ancestors, Shpitser's district formula with it) and evaluated by the finite-discrete functional plug-in or its Bayesian-bootstrap posterior. A mediator-outcome, treatment-mediator or treatment-outcome latent confounder leaves a recanting district or a district kernel with a hedge, and the effect is refused as not identified. The result keeps support status refused: no evidence row or coverage record names the cell.
NestedCounterfactualEffect on a mixed graph, a Cpdag or a Pag is staged for an explicit or accepted graph; graph-posterior mixing over its atoms is not.
NestedCounterfactualEffect has no compatible cheap/full cross-world refuter suite.
NestedCounterfactualEffect requires an explicitly supplied Dag; accepted and graph-posterior structures are not licensed.
NestedCounterfactualEffect has no compatible cheap/full cross-world refuter suite.
Staged counterfactuals require a supplied Dag; graph-posterior structures are refused.
Counterfactual cheap/full are not licensed; there is no native ITE refuter suite and ATE refuters do not apply.

Graph-posterior ResponseCurve on Admg/TemporalAdmg/Cpdag/Pag is licensed at validation none. cheap/full name the ATE-shaped scalar refuter suite; the curve remains function-valued or atom-mixed with no licensed scalar-refuter state.

A pulse, sustained or conditional contrast on one series under a TemporalAdmg is identified on the unrolled window of its template: the template is unrolled over the periods the policy needs (a cause that precedes the window is a latent common cause of its in-window effects), the complete ID algorithm identifies both sides of the contrast (IDC with the modifiers read at the first treated period for a conditional contrast), and the identified functional is evaluated by the discrete plug-in on the lag-aligned window table. Frequentist uncertainty resamples circular blocks of consecutive windows and Bayesian uncertainty shares one Dirichlet weight per block, never shorter than the window, because overlapping windows invalidate a row-level draw; the series is read as stationary over the template. Cheap validation refits the plug-in on a random contiguous stretch of 80% of the windows and rotates the treatment columns together by at least one window, which must give a contrast indistinguishable from zero; full validation adds a 50% stretch and a split-half stationarity test (the contrast on the first half of the windows against the second, each with a circular-block bootstrap standard error). Both inference modes run the same window-native suite on the plug-in. The result keeps support status refused and discloses estimate.temporal_admg.window; no evidence row or coverage record names the cell. A window that holds a hedge is refused with the variables and periods that carry it, and a modifier a treated period can reach is refused. Discrete data only.

The window contrast on a TemporalAdmg (the rule above) reads one supplied or accepted template. A graph posterior over TemporalAdmg atoms is a posterior over contemporaneous adjacency and has no lagged-template atoms to unroll, so it has no window route. Next attempts: a supplied or accepted TemporalAdmg, or a TemporalDag when the lag structure has no latent confounding.

A temporal mediation contrast on TemporalAdmg is a cross-world contrast: the window-unrolled identification covers interventional contrasts only, and the recanting-district criterion for path-specific effects has not been derived on the unrolled window. Next attempts: TemporalMediationEffect on a TemporalDag or TemporalCpdag, or the pulse or sustained contrast on the TemporalAdmg, which executes unlicensed.
Graph-posterior temporal conditional effects on a TemporalDag are not licensed.
A temporal conditional effect has no scalar ATE refuter; cheap and full are not licensed.
Graph-posterior temporal derivatives on a TemporalDag are not licensed.
Graph-posterior temporal cross-world effects on a TemporalDag are not licensed.
Temporal cross-world effects are point-only; cheap and full are not licensed.
Graph-posterior temporal derivatives on TemporalCpdag and TemporalPag are licensed at validation none. Derivative-native cheap/full validation is not implemented; ATE refuters do not apply.
Graph-posterior temporal cross-world effects on TemporalCpdag and TemporalPag are point-only; cheap and full are not licensed.

Graph-posterior temporal conditional effects on TemporalCpdag and TemporalPag are licensed at validation none. A temporal conditional effect has no scalar ATE refuter; cheap and full are not licensed.
